points.title: 贵族童年
points.description: 托马斯·阿奎那出生于意大利罗卡塞卡城堡，是伦巴第地区阿奎那伯爵的第九子。作为贵族子弟，他从小接受了良好的基础教育，但五岁时被送往本笃会的蒙特卡西诺修道院接受预备教育，为日后成为神职人员做准备。这段贵族家庭背景和早期修道院教育塑造了他后来的思想体系，融合了亚里士多德哲学与基督教神学的基础。
points.descriptionEn: Thomas Aquinas was born in Roccasecca Castle, Italy, as the ninth son of Count Landulf of Aquino. As a noble child, he received excellent early education. At age five, he was sent to Monte Cassino Abbey for preparatory education, preparing him for future clerical life. This noble background and early monastic education shaped his later philosophical system, which integrated Aristotelian philosophy with Christian theology.

points.title: 求学启蒙
points.description: 托马斯进入那不勒斯大学学习，接触到了亚里士多德的著作以及阿拉伯哲学家的注释。在这里，他接触到了当时最前沿的知识，包括逻辑学、自然科学和哲学。这段学习经历为他后来的思想体系奠定了基础，但也使他开始质疑传统奥古斯丁主义的某些观点。1244年，他不顾家族反对，加入了多明我会，这一决定激怒了他的家人，甚至被绑架囚禁了一年。
points.descriptionEn: Thomas entered the University of Naples, where he studied Aristotle's works and commentaries by Arab philosophers. Here, he was exposed to cutting-edge knowledge including logic, natural sciences, and philosophy. This period laid the foundation for his later philosophical system but also led him to question certain aspects of traditional Augustinianism. In 1244, against his family's wishes, he joined the Dominican Order, a decision that angered his family, leading to his kidnapping and imprisonment for a year.

points.title: 神学深造
points.description: 托马斯前往巴黎大学，在阿尔伯特·马格努斯指导下学习神学和哲学。这段时期他系统研究了亚里士多德的著作，并尝试将其思想与基督教教义调和。1252年，他开始在巴黎大学担任神学教师，开始讲授《圣经》和彼得·伦巴德的《箴言四书》。这一阶段标志着他神学思想体系的初步形成，也为他后来撰写《神学大全》奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Thomas went to the University of Paris, studying theology and philosophy under Albertus Magnus. During this period, he systematically studied Aristotle's works and attempted to reconcile his ideas with Christian doctrine. In 1252, he began teaching theology at the University of Paris, lecturing on the Bible and Peter Lombard's 'Sentences'. This period marked the initial formation of his theological system and laid the foundation for his later 'Summa Theologica'.

points.title: 学术巅峰
points.description: 1256年，托马斯获得神学博士学位，开始在巴黎大学担任教授。这一时期，他完成了《反异教大全》的大部分内容，并开始撰写《神学大全》。他还参与了巴黎大学的学术辩论，特别是关于亚里士多德哲学与基督教教义调和的讨论。1268年，他回到巴黎，面对巴黎主教对亚里士多德哲学的谴责，托马斯坚持认为亚里士多德的思想可以与基督教教义调和，这一立场使他成为当时神学界的领军人物。
points.descriptionEn: In 1256, Thomas received his doctorate in theology and began teaching at the University of Paris. During this period, he completed most of 'Summa Contra Gentiles' and began writing 'Summa Theologica'. He participated in academic debates at the university, particularly regarding the reconciliation of Aristotelian philosophy with Christian doctrine. In 1268, he returned to Paris, facing condemnation of Aristotelian philosophy by the Bishop of Paris. Thomas insisted that Aristotle's ideas could be reconciled with Christian doctrine, establishing him as a leading figure in contemporary theology.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 1272年，托马斯回到那不勒斯，担任多明我会修道院院长，并继续他的神学研究。这一时期，他完成了《神学大全》的第二部分，并开始撰写第三部分。1274年，他参加里昂大公会议途中，在福萨的西斯特尔诺本笃会修道院逝世，享年49岁。他的去世被视为天主教的一大损失，但他的思想遗产却影响深远。他的著作被整合进天主教教义，成为托马斯主义的基础，影响了整个中世纪晚期及近代早期的神学和哲学发展。
points.descriptionEn: In 1272, Thomas returned to Naples, serving as prior of the Dominican monastery and continuing his theological research. During this period, he completed the second part of 'Summa Theologica' and began writing the third part. In 1274, on his way to the Second Council of Lyon, he died at the Cistercian Abbey of Fossanova at age 49. His death was seen as a great loss to Catholicism, but his intellectual legacy had profound influence. His works were integrated into Catholic doctrine, forming the foundation of Thomism, influencing theological and philosophical development in the late Middle Ages and early modern period.

supporter.zh: 托马斯·阿奎那被尊为天主教最伟大的神学家和哲学家之一，他的托马斯主义成为天主教官方哲学。他成功地将亚里士多德的哲学思想与基督教教义调和，为信仰与理性提供了和谐统一的框架。他的《神学大全》被视为神学思想的巅峰之作，对后世神学、哲学和法律产生了深远影响。阿奎那的'自然法'理论为现代人权观念奠定了基础，他的'五路证明'成为论证上帝存在的经典方法。
supporter.en: Thomas Aquinas is revered as one of the greatest theologians and philosophers in Catholic history, with Thomism becoming the official philosophy of the Church. He successfully reconciled Aristotelian philosophy with Christian doctrine, providing a harmonious framework for faith and reason. His 'Summa Theologica' is considered the pinnacle of theological thought, profoundly influencing subsequent theology, philosophy, and law. Aquinas's theory of natural law laid the foundation for modern human rights concepts, and his 'Five Ways' remain classic arguments for God's existence.

critic.zh: 批评者认为阿奎那过度依赖亚里士多德哲学，导致基督教信仰被理性主义所束缚。他的神学体系被认为过于复杂和抽象，脱离了普通信徒的信仰体验。一些现代神学家批评他的'类比说'限制了上帝超越性的理解，而他的'自然法'理论被指责为可能为不平等的社会秩序提供神学辩护。此外，阿奎那对异端和犹太教的强硬态度也受到现代多元主义思想的质疑。
critic.en: Critics argue that Aquinas's excessive reliance on Aristotelian philosophy constrained Christian faith within rationalism. His theological system is seen as overly complex and abstract, detached from the faith experiences of ordinary believers. Some modern theologians criticize his 'analogy of being' as limiting the understanding of God's transcendence, and his natural law theory is accused of potentially providing theological justification for unequal social orders. Additionally, his harsh stance toward heretics and Jews is questioned by modern pluralistic thought.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，阿奎那被视为中世纪思想的集大成者，他代表了理性与信仰调和的尝试。他的思想既影响了经院哲学的发展，也为后来的文艺复兴和启蒙运动提供了思想资源。在流行文化中，阿奎那常被描绘为理性与信仰平衡的象征，他的形象出现在各种艺术作品和学术讨论中。现代学术界对他的研究已超越神学领域，延伸到伦理学、政治哲学和认识论等多个学科，显示出其思想的持久生命力。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Aquinas is regarded as the culmination of medieval thought, representing an attempt to reconcile reason and faith. His ideas influenced both the development of scholastic philosophy and provided intellectual resources for later Renaissance and Enlightenment movements. In popular culture, Aquinas is often depicted as a symbol of balance between reason and faith, appearing in various artistic works and academic discussions. Modern academic research on Aquinas has extended beyond theology into ethics, political philosophy, and epistemology, demonstrating the enduring vitality of his thought.

self.zh: 恩典并不废除自然，而是成全自然。
self.en: Grace does not destroy nature, but perfects it.

others.zh: 阿奎那是所有基督教哲学家中最伟大的，也是所有哲学家中最基督教的。
others.en: Aquinas is the greatest of all Christian philosophers and the most Christian of all philosophers.
